one_liner: Rust crate generating simplex, FBM, ridge, turbulence and cellular noise with SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2 runtime dispatch; beats its own 1-lane scalar path.
what_it_does: Generates 1D-4D gradient (simplex) noise, fractal Brownian motion, ridge and turbulence fractals, and 2D/3D cellular (Voronoi) noise. The main API is a builder (NoiseBuilder::fbm_2d(w, h).with_octaves(..).generate() or generate_scaled(min, max)) that fills a Vec<f32> block and returns the raw min and max for scaling. Lower-level per-vector functions in simdnoise::intrinsics::{scalar, sse2, sse41, avx2} take and return SIMD registers for custom sampling patterns such as points on a sphere. It is its own API, not a drop-in for the noise crate or any C++ library.
how_it_is_fast: Each noise function is written once as generic code over simdeez's Simd trait and instantiated for SSE2 (4 lanes), SSE4.1 (4 lanes) and AVX2 with FMA3 (8 lanes); block generation walks the grid a full vector of x coordinates at a time and keeps running min/max in registers. The top-level get_*_noise functions use simdeez's simd_runtime_generate! macro, which checks is_x86_feature_detected! once and runs the body inside a #[target_feature]-enabled closure so the intrinsics inline. The 'scalar' path is the same generic code on simdeez's 1-lane Scalar engine, not a separately tuned scalar implementation.
when_to_use: Pure-Rust procedural content (terrain heightmaps, textures, voxel density fields) on x86-64 where whole 2D or 3D blocks of FBM, ridge, turbulence or cellular noise are generated at once.
Large single-threaded blocks such as a 3840 x 2160 FBM map or a 128^3 cellular volume, where the README reports 8.2x (FBM) and 29.8x (cellular) over the crate's scalar path with AVX2.
Projects that want automatic SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2 selection at runtime without shipping separate binaries.
Callers that already hold SIMD registers and want per-vector noise evaluation through the intrinsics module, wrapped in their own #[target_feature] function.
when_not_to_use: C++ codebases: there is no C or C++ API, and FastNoise2 is the native C++ SIMD option with comparisons against independent libraries.

ARM or Apple Silicon targets that need SIMD speed: NEON and AVX-512 are TODO; HEAD falls back to scalar on aarch64, and the published 3.1.6 crate fails to compile on an M1 (issue #52, error E0425 for F32x4 in sse41.rs).

Anyone who needs a maintained crates.io release: crates.io still serves 3.1.6 (2020-05-30, simdeez ^1.0.3); HEAD 3.1.7 is unpublished and pins the prerelease simdeez 2.0.0-dev3 although simdeez 2.0.0 and 3.0.1 are out; issue #35 'crates.io release' has been open since 2021.

Workloads that need seamless or artifact-free output without checking: open issues report seams at high octaves and low frequency (#39), grid-like artifacts in turbulence_3d (#15), Cellular2 3D resetting when z changes (#37) and weak seed randomness (#42).
Windows MSVC builds of 3D AVX2 noise from git HEAD: issue #38 reports a stack overflow (forced #[inline(always)] creates a single frame above the __chkstk limit); the 3.1.6 release is not affected.

integration.dependencies: simdeez 2.0.0-dev3 at HEAD (prerelease pin); simdeez ^1.0.3 in the published 3.1.6
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2018, stable rustc (CI builds on stable); MSRV not documented
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 with SSE2, SSE4.1 or AVX2+FMA3 picked at runtime; other targets use the scalar engine at HEAD only
integration.thread_safety: not documented; generators are pure functions that take settings by value or reference, read static permutation tables and return a new Vec, so concurrent calls look safe, but the project does not state it

gotchas: Harness flaw at HEAD: since the November 2024 simdeez v2 port, simdnoise::intrinsics::{sse41,avx2}::get_*_noise are plain generic functions without #[target_feature], while simdeez 2.0.0-dev3 marks every AVX2/SSE4.1 op #[inline] #[target_feature(enable = ...)]; benches/benchmarks.rs calls them straight from Criterion closures (the repo's own tests wrap each call in a #[target_feature] function) and the repo has no RUSTFLAGS or .cargo/config (removed 2024-11-19), so a default cargo bench at HEAD likely times out-of-line op calls for the sse41 and avx2 rows (not run here). The README table is not from this harness: it first appears in commit 498bf3d (2019-03-05), when the avx2 entry points carried #[target_feature(enable = "avx2")].

The baseline is simdeez's 1-lane Scalar engine running the same generic SIMD code (the 2019 scalar.rs instantiates cellular_3d::<Scalar> on F32x1), not a hand-written scalar generator or a third-party library; the superlinear 10.9x SSE2 gain on 4 lanes for 3D cellular noise points to emulation overhead in that path. Earlier README tables on the same i7-6700 (June-July 2018) showed only 3.6-6.7x for AVX2 FBM. The committed golden outputs at HEAD agree between scalar and SIMD paths within 8.7e-5 (3D cellular) and 1.9e-6 (2D FBM), derived from tests/assets, so the paths do compute the same function.

fbm_1d (f32 and f64) updates amp each octave but never multiplies the octave by it, so 1D FBM ignores the gain setting while the 2D-4D versions apply it (fbm_4d itself was fixed in 2024 for using only 3 dimensions).

Tests lock in current output rather than cross-checking paths: the scalar-versus-SIMD consistency tests in src/lib.rs are commented out, test assets were regenerated on 2024-11-18 ('accept current implementation as-is'), four f64 SSE2 tests are #[ignore]d, and the README's 'call noise functions directly' example uses pre-port signatures (no ::<S> type argument, simplex_2d without seed) that do not compile against HEAD.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick SIMDNoise over FastNoise2 only when you need pure Rust without a C++ build or FFI layer and x86 SSE2/AVX2 is enough; FastNoise2 has more noise types, ARM NEON and AVX-512 support, and benchmarks against independent libraries (FastNoise Lite, libnoise, stb_perlin) rather than its own scalar path.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README table, added in commit 498bf3d (2019-03-05) by Jack Mott: on an i7-6700, single-threaded, Criterion.rs, rustc and RUSTFLAGS not stated, a 3840 x 2160 3-octave FBM block takes 888 ms on the crate's scalar path versus 108 ms with AVX2 (about 8.2x) and a 128^3 cellular block 1,400 ms versus 47 ms (about 29.8x), derived from page data. The baseline is the same generic code on simdeez's 1-lane Scalar engine, and the numbers predate the 3.1.x releases (August 2019 onward) and the November 2024 simdeez v2 port.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2024-11-20, 'port benchmarks to simdeez v2'; latest crates.io release 3.1.6 from 2020-05-30, about 81k downloads), dual Apache-2.0/MIT declared only in Cargo.toml, and HEAD depends on a simdeez prerelease, so pin a git revision or vendor it and benchmark your own block sizes.
